verdict.rationale: Glama documents publishing your own server. You connect a GitHub repo or ship a Dockerfile, npm or PyPI package, Glama builds it, and you flip it from private to a public listing. Ownership is verified via a claim token, and registry pages give others pre-filled install configs. Community developers confirm uploading their own MCPs and releasing new versions, though one hit an undocumented credit-card requirement for rebuilds and releases. missing for 10: a documented end-to-end submission/listing workflow, documentation of billing prerequisites for rebuild/release, and evidence of discoverability or promotion support for newly listed servers.

support.subject: As a developer, I can publish my own MCP server on the platform for distribution, discovery, and installation by others

citations.quote: Connect a GitHub repository and Glama builds the image straight from source.
Ship a Dockerfile, an npm package, or a PyPI module.
Private by default – flip to public listing when ready.
Stable, account-bound ownership token copied from the Glama claim panel. Keep it published to retain verified ownership.
Every server on the Glama registry ships with a pre-filled config block for both clients – copy it, paste it, done.
I've personally revised my MCPs to improve the quality of the score
